ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001, as amended by the Financial Intelligence Centre Amendment Act 1 of 2017 and the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorist Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022; Companies Act 71 of 2008, as amended by the Companies Amendment Act 16 of 2023; Companies Regulations, 2011, as amended, including CIPC Beneficial Ownership Register obligations; Protection of Constitutional Democracy against Terrorist and Related Activities Act 33 of 2004; Financial Action Task Force Recommendations as implemented by the Financial Intelligence Centre.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (CIPC, Financial Intelligence Centre, South African Reserve Bank, SARS and law-enforcement agencies, with lawful access gateways; not a publicly searchable register)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent passport or identity authority in the individual's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if issuing country is an Apostille party; otherwise consular legalization by a South African embassy, High Commission or consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Recent proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement) for each UBO, director and proposed shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing utility company or regulated bank in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; sworn English translation if the issue language is not English

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incumbency or company extract for any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign company registry or registered agent in the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, with certified English translation if necessary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney appointing the South African incorporation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public competent in the jurisdiction of execution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the executing country is a party; otherwise consular legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs, signatories and officers against the FIC targeted financial sanctions lists, UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List and domestic PEP databases, including close associates and family members; ongoing transaction monitoring and risk-based enhanced due diligence for domestic and foreign prominent influential persons under FICA; negative-match documentation and screening-date evidence must be retained.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Proposed names may be in any of the eleven official South African languages or in English; names in non-Latin scripts must be transliterated to the Latin or Roman alphabet; the legal suffix must be 'Proprietary Limited' or '(Pty) Ltd' and must be stated in the reservation application; a foreign-language name must be accompanied by an English transliteration or translation for CIPC register purposes.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If CIPC rejects the proposed name on grounds of confusing similarity, undesirability or non-compliance, the applicant may apply to the Companies Tribunal under section 10(2) of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 and the Companies Regulations, 2011, by filing a notice of motion and supporting affidavit against the Commission and paying the prescribed Tribunal fee. The Tribunal may confirm, set aside or vary the CIPC decision, and any further administrative-review challenge may be brought to the High Court under the Promotion of Administrative Justice Act 3 of 2000. Rejections based on the absence of required regulatory consent must first be cured by obtaining and attaching the relevant SARB or FSCA approval and re-filing the name. A reserved name may be renewed for a further six-month period before expiry; once expired, a fresh name-reservation application is required.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as the sole statutory arrangement for this high-risk financial-services entity. CIPC requires a physical registered office address in South Africa; the FIC Act and SARB's National Payment System Department require the licensed issuer to maintain a physical operational place of business and supporting records in South Africa. A virtual office may only supplement, not replace, the physical registered office and operational premises.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated 85% within the first 24 months of FIC/regulatory registration and licensing: unannounced on-site inspections and record inspections are routinely conducted by the Financial Intelligence Centre, the South African Reserve Bank, and the Financial Sector Conduct Authority for virtual card issuers and fintech accountable institutions.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act No. 71 of 2008, as amended by the Companies Amendment Act No. 16 of 2024: sections 13 (incorporation), 14 (registration), 15 (memorandum of incorporation), 19 (separate legal personality) and 40 (issue of shares).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), an autonomous agency of the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (the dtic), with head office in Pretoria, Gauteng.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) accompanied by the Memorandum of Incorporation (standard private-company form CoR 15.1 or a bespoke MOI) lodged on the CIPC e-Services portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital or escrow-account obligation applies to a Proprietary Limited company under the Companies Act 71 of 2008; shares may be issued fully or partly paid at the par value selected in the MOI. However, the virtual-card float must be segregated in a client-money account held with a licensed commercial bank as a National Payment System Act practice requirement before card issuance commences.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the incorporation of the company under section 14 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008, evidenced by the certificate of the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission, be accepted and the Memorandum of Incorporation adopted. RESOLVED FURTHER that the authorised ordinary shares be allotted to the founding subscribers as set out in the subscription schedule and the share register opened accordingly. RESOLVED FURTHER that the registered office be established at the address recorded in the Notice of Incorporation. RESOLVED FURTHER that [Name] be appointed Director, [Name] Chief Executive Officer and [Name] Company Secretary, each authorised to open bank accounts and to file all licence applications with the South African Reserve Bank and the Financial Sector Conduct Authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) e-Services portal, name-reservation module (www.cipc.co.za)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log on to the CIPC e-Services portal with the practitioner profile of an attorney or corporate constitutive practitioner; complete Form CoR 9.1 requesting reservation of the proposed company name; pay the R50 name-reservation fee; retain the reservation reference number which remains valid for six months. If the company elects to trade under its enterprise number, proceed directly to Step 3.
required_dossiers: Certified copies of identity documents or passports of the incorporators
Optional: trademark and company-name search confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the name is objected to or rejected by CIPC, the practitioner may file a fresh name reservation with a revised name or escalate a written motivation within 10 business days; the rejected reference is closed and a new reservation is opened without prejudice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Memorandum of Incorporation and Notice of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC e-Services document lodgement; notarial execution for foreign incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the MOI using CIPC standard Form CoR 15.1 for a private company or a bespoke MOI defining share classes, board quorum and transfer restrictions; execute it together with the Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) by the incorporators; where incorporators are outside South Africa, notarise and apostille the execution pages under the Hague Apostille Convention.
required_dossiers: Certified ID/passport copies of all incorporators
Apostilled execution pages where foreign parties execute
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC raises a query on the MOI clauses (e.g., prohibited promoter provisions or a name inconsistency), the practitioner must submit the corrective CoR 24 filing and an amended MOI within the 10-business-day query window; no re-notarisation is required unless the amendment alters execution rights.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Lodgement, Payment of Fee and CIPC Adjudication
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the executed CoR 14.1, the MOI and supporting dossiers to the CIPC e-Services portal; pay the R425 incorporation registration fee for a private company by credit card or electronic funds transfer; the automated adjudication engine validates the MOI fields, name reservation reference, director eligibility and disclosed share capital before registration is recommended.
required_dossiers: Beneficial-ownership schedule as required on incorporation
Proof of payment of the incorporation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where a compliance notice or pending status is returned, the practitioner must correct the contested fields and resubmit the lodgement within 10 business days of the notice; automated de-registration is not triggered during the pendency.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issue of the Certificate of Incorporation and Enterprise Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Download the electronic Certificate of Incorporation from the e-Services transaction history; verify the company's separate juristic personality date under section 19 of the Companies Act, the incorporation date, and the assigned enterprise number; the MOI and certificate are then filed in the company's statutory records file.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is not generated within 20 business days, the practitioner may escalate the pending reference via the CIPC enquiries queue or direct correspondence to the CIPC Registration Office head; reconciliation of the payment reference normally unblocks the file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting and Adoption of Corporate Governance Instruments
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first meeting of the board at the registered office or via a meeting by electronic communication; adopt the Pro-Forma First Board Resolution covering adoption of the MOI, allotment of shares, establishment of the registered office and appointment of officers; approve the minute book, share register and registers of directors and prescribed officers.
required_dossiers: Notice convening the first board meeting
Consent-to-act and acceptance letters of directors and officers
Minutes of the first board meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where a quorum cannot be formed, the meeting is adjourned and reconvened after seven days; alternatively, the resolution may be passed by written assent of all shareholders in lieu of a meeting under section 67 of the Companies Act.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) - eFiling portal at www.sarsefiling.co.za; entity incorporation must first be completed through the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) with subsequent SARS tax registration
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign parent must incorporate a South African Proprietary Limited (Pty) Ltd through CIPC, then register the company with SARS on eFiling to obtain an Income Tax Reference Number. Non-resident companies with a South African permanent establishment must register for income tax and obtain a SARS income tax reference number. VAT registration is a separate SARS application (VAT 101 form) with compulsory registration where taxable supplies exceed ZAR 1,000,000 in any 12-month period, or voluntary registration where taxable supplies exceed ZAR 50,000 in 12 months. The company must also register for Pay-As-You-Earn (PAYE), UIF, and SDL as an employer if it has employees. SARS will issue a single tax reference number linked to the company profile which is used for income tax, VAT, customs, and other administered Acts.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election is available in South Africa. Taxation follows residence and source principles under the Income Tax Act 58 of 1962. A resident company is taxed on worldwide income at a standard corporate rate of 27%; non-resident companies are taxed on South African-source income only if they have a permanent establishment. Qualifying small business corporations with all natural-person shareholders and gross income below ZAR 20 million may elect graduated rates under s12E. VAT group registration may be elected under s50(1) of the VAT Act for 100%-owned group companies to consolidate VAT accounting. Tax consolidation (group relief) under s41 of the Income Tax Act is available for 70%+ subsidiaries with a formal group election. Hybrid mismatch rules apply under s25N and align with OECD BEPS Action 2, limiting elective mechanisms that create double non-taxation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991, administered by SARS; no provincial sales tax applies in South Africa
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory registration threshold: ZAR 1,000,000 in taxable supplies made in any 12-month rolling period. Voluntary registration threshold: ZAR 50,000 in taxable supplies in any 12-month period (subject to SARS discretion). Foreign vendors carrying on a business in South Africa and making taxable supplies are subject to the same thresholds and may be required to register from the first supply.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: South Africa does not currently mandate a real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, or digital stamping regime comparable to Italy or Mexico. Electronic VAT invoices are legally valid if they contain all prescribed particulars under s20(4) of the VAT Act, including vendor name, VAT registration number, invoice description, quantity, price, and tax amount. SARS publishes a Digital Tax Register interface specification and increasingly uses eFiling data integration to cross-match transactional data; SARS is actively expanding e-invoicing adoption; however, there is no mandatory API-based clearance token or real-time XML approval as at the current effective regime. Vendors are required to retain all electronic and documentary records for at least five years and must keep them available to SARS on request.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A zero-rate of 0% VAT applies to the export of movable goods under s11(1)(a) of the VAT Act provided the supplier has exported the goods within the prescribed period and retains the required documentary proof. Services may be zero-rated under s11(2)(l) where the services are supplied to a non-resident who is not in South Africa at the time of supply and the services are not used or consumed in South Africa. For a virtual card issuer supplying B2B card-issuing and spend-management services to non-resident counterparties, zero-rating of exported services is available if the supply is not exempt financial services; the supplier should obtain a specific SARS VAT ruling because card-issuing and payment processing may constitute exempt financial services under s2 of the VAT Act, and the exemption/zero-rating boundary is narrow. The company must demonstrate that the recipient is a non-resident, the services are performed for a foreign market, and the services are not connected to South African land, goods, or improvement. Goods exported by the company itself or on the company's behalf are zero-rated only when physical removal from South Africa is completed and proof of export is retained.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD 500 digitally lodged through SARS Customs and eFiling)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical export from South Africa
Proof of payment from the foreign buyer, including a Foreign Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or bank SWIFT confirmation
Transport or freight documentation and insurance certificates supporting the export movement
Contract or purchase order confirming the non-resident status of the recipient
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS has enhanced export verification and refund risk profiling. Where an exporter fails to export goods within the prescribed period or cannot substantiate the export documentation bundle, SARS will reverse the zero-rating, assess output VAT at 15%, impose interest under s187 of the Tax Administration Act, and may impose an understatement penalty under s223 of between 0% and 150% of the shortfall depending on the conduct classification. In cases of intentional tax evasion, s60 of the VAT Act permits additional tax of up to 100% of the tax evaded, and criminal prosecution may result in a fine or imprisonment. SARS may also claw back credited input VAT, set off refunds, and apply a 'no export, no refund' approach, with retrospective assessments stretching back up to five years, or unlimited in cases of fraud. Payment service and card-issuing exporters claiming zero-rated services must maintain full audit trails of the foreign counterparty, the place of consumption, and the foreign currency settlement to avoid retrospective clawbacks.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB) - Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv), acting as Exchange Control Authority under the Currency and Exchanges Act 9 of 1933
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The South African rand is a regulated convertible currency: current account payments are presumptively permissible through authorised dealers with documented underlying commercial transactions, while capital account transactions are liberalised only within prescribed limits and thresholds. Profit remittances and dividend distributions to non-resident shareholders require an audited or reviewed annual financial statement, SARS tax clearance (tax compliance status), board resolution, and proof of beneficial ownership filing; remittance is processed with withholding tax (Dividends Tax) and exchange-control verification. The principal hurdles are documentary completeness, SARS compliance status, and SARB FinSurv reporting obligations rather than outright remittance prohibition. Non-resident equity injections are generally permitted through authorised dealers as inward listings, but related-party loans and subsequent capital account conversions may require evidence of trade/investment bona fides and, if above regulatory thresholds, FinSurv approval.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Exporters must ensure foreign-currency export proceeds are received in South Africa within 180 days of shipment (or within an extended period granted by an authorised dealer/FinSurv for valid commercial reasons); once received, the proceeds must be surrendered by selling the foreign currency to an authorised dealer within 30 days. The mandatory conversion ratio is effectively 100% of repatriated export receipts, denominated in a negotiable currency, converted into rand unless a specific exemption (e.g., offsetting foreign trade financing or unavoidable offshore retention) has been granted in writing. All export documentation must be retained for 5 years and produced to the authorised dealer/SARB upon request.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: The Standard Bank of South Africa Limited

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to Medium viability for an offshore digital EMI: South Africa has no passporting regime for foreign electronic-money institutions; any card-issuing/payment processing business requires either a banking licence under the Banks Act, a payment-service-provider authorisation under the National Payment System Act, or a material outsourcing arrangement with a licensed South African clearing bank. Offshore EMIs can serve only as payment-facilitation or treasury-reconciliation layers, not as onshore deposit-taking or direct scheme-member entities. Credit risk, AML/CFT accountability under the Financial Intelligence Centre Act (FIC Act), and scheme rules (Visa/Mastercard) require onshore legal substance and a sponsor bank or principal membership.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: South African FIC Act does not expressly prescribe physical attendance for all account openings, but banks applying a risk-based approach for a high-risk fintech issuer will in practice require a physical due-diligence interview of at least one executive director and the Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) at the bank's corporate office or via an approved remote-video onboarding channel with notarised/certified copies. For higher-risk structures, a branch or corporate adviser appointment is normally mandatory for first set-up; subsequent files can be managed electronically. Directors should expect biometric verification, electronic verification via home-affairs records, and the production of certified board resolutions and constitutional documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained beneficial ownership or non-transparent multi-jurisdictional ownership chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate diagram showing all entities and UBOs; CIPC certificates; registry extracts or equivalent foreign jurisdictional filings; beneficial-ownership register filed with the Beneficial Ownership Information portal; sworn declarations and descriptions of economic substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds for the capital injection / share subscription
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements, bank statements of the investing entity, tax clearance certificates in the investor jurisdiction, board resolutions, share subscription agreements, evidence of bank wiring instructions from the investor's named account, and signed declarations of source of wealth.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction exposure, sanction screening hit or PEP status of shareholders/directors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Screening output logs, full explanation of any name-only match, professional/legal references, citizenship/residency proof, regulatory clearance letters, and, where relevant, enhanced due-diligence questionnaires approved by the AML officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Card issuance/receivables business perceived as money-laundering or consumer-credit risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business model memorandum, product flow diagram, program manager agreement, card scheme membership/BIN sponsorship letter, merchant and cardholder AML policies, transaction monitoring procedures, FIC Act registration number, and independent audit report on internal controls.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inability to identify the card program sponsor or payment-network authorisation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed sponsor-bank agreement; scheme approval correspondence; legal opinion confirming no unauthorised deposit-taking; and a ring-fenced client-funds/treasury structure demonstrating that virtual-card liabilities are supported by segregated settlement balances.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity investment must be routed through an authorised dealer in South Africa by SWIFT MT103/202 for the credit of the (Pty) Ltd's operational or capital escrow account, referencing the share certificate/CIPC confirmation and a clearly stated payment narrative reading 'Equity subscription - ZA PTY LTD'. The authorised dealer must be furnished with the inward listing (FDI) notification information, proof of incorporation, share allotment resolution, and a copy of the bank's KYC/AML analysis. For foreign direct investment into ordinary shares, the bank will apply the applicable ZAR/BOP purpose classification (direct investment equity - inward), and no SARB prior approval is required for a standard private company equity injection from an arm's-length non-resident shareholder. Proceeds may be invested in interest-bearing call or money-market instruments pending deployment, but the company must ensure the funds are not used for prohibited speculative FX activity. If the subscription includes a share premium or an intercompany shareholder loan, additional financing documentation and FIC Act source-of-funds evidence must be provided to avoid being treated as a regulated borrowing.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements are to be made via SA-SWIFT MT103 for direct payments of card-scheme network and vendor/merchant invoices, and via commercial letters of credit (documentary L/Cs) issued by a domestic authorised dealer for high-value cross-border procurement of card production equipment or software licensing. The company must use authorised-dealer clearing channels for all ZAR-denominated outbound automated clearing (ACB/DeR) transactions. For the card business specifically, outbound settlement between the card issuer, principal member/sponsor bank, and Mastercard/Visa clearing systems must be settled through the sponsor bank's card-scheme settlement platform or a licensed payment-clearing house; the domestic card network accounts must be segregated and reconciled daily. All payments must carry a correct BOP purpose code and supporting transaction documents (invoices, contracts, scheme settlement reports) to facilitate the dealer's exchange-control verification; beneficiary bank and IBAN/account-holder exactness must be validated to avoid return/rejects.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward Exchange Contract (FEC) executed through an authorised dealer for firm commercial commitments (e.g., buying card hardware or software licences in USD/EUR)

Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF) used only where the hedge is linked to an offshore reference currency and settlement cannot be physically converted in the required period; subject to dealer's documented underlying exposure
Cross-Currency Interest-Rate Swap (CCIRS) or Currency Swap with an authorised dealer for long-term capital/refinancing and settlement-risk hedging
FX option (vanilla put/call) via an authorised dealer for contingent tender/renewal exposures, subject to FEC/option documentation and underlying transaction proof
Outright spot/forward trades in the interbank market through the dealer for operational currency flows; not for speculative treasury profit-taking

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), Department of Trade, Industry and Competition
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after the anniversary of the company's date of incorporation, filed annually via CIPC e-filing.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing: ZAR 250 penalty if more than 30 business days overdue, increasing to ZAR 500 after 40 business days; two consecutive years of non-filing permits CIPC administrative strike-off (deregistration) under s.82(3) of the Companies Act following a Gazette notice; company loses certificate of good standing and directors may face personal liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: CIPC Beneficial Ownership Module (General Laws AML/CTF Amendment Act 22 of 2022)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation submitted together with the CIPC Annual Return; any shareholding transfer changing beneficial ownership must be filed within 10 business days of the transaction.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Omission or false declaration is a criminal offence; CIPC may impose administrative penalties, reject the annual return, and withhold compliance certificates; directors risk personal prosecution; non-compliance is also a supervisory breach before SARB/FIC.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Annual Financial Statements (IFRS) and Regulatory Submission
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: SARB Prudential Authority (National Payment System Department); CIPC where statutory AFS filing applies; board of directors
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after financial year-end (Companies Act s.30(1)); SARB submission follows the National Payment System Act licence annual reporting condition.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Breach of the SARB licence condition and s.30/s.31 Companies Act; CIPC compliance notice and administrative fines on directors; SARB enforcement action may include suspension or withdrawal of the card-issuing licence.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (ITR14) and Provisional Tax Schedule
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: ITR14 due within 12 months of financial year-end via e-filing; provisional tax payments due at month 6 and month 12 of the tax year, with an optional top-up by month 18.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing administrative penalties and prescribed interest under the Tax Administration Act; understatement penalties up to 200% of the tax shortfall for intentional misdeclarations; directors may face personal liability for wilful non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: FIC Risk and Compliance Return (RCR) - AML/CFT Annual Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 30 days after the end of the accountable institution's financial year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Contravention is an offence under the FIC Act; FIC administrative sanctions may reach ZAR 10 million per breach plus daily penalties; SARB treats non-filing as a licence supervisory breach.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% for years of assessment commencing on or after 1 April 2022; the predecessor rate was 28%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday or dividend-trade exemption applies to a standard (Pty) Ltd. Qualifying capital expenditure on cost-incurring commercial assets may be accelerated under s12C of the Income Tax Act 58 of 1962, and qualifying research and development expenditure may be deductible under s11D. The effective rate may be reduced in practice by assessed losses carried forward from prior years, allowable deductions and available Foreign Tax Credits, but no executive or industrial zone tax holiday applies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ITR14 (Company Income Tax Return for companies) filed electronically through the SARS eFiling portal at https://www.sarsefiling.co.za
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: ITR14 must be submitted within 12 months after the company's financial year-end. Provisional tax payments are due as follows: first provisional payment six months after the start of the year of assessment; second provisional payment on or before the last business day of the year of assessment; third top-up provisional payment within six months after the financial year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross receipts and accruals derived from virtual card issuing, interchange fees, annual card fees, foreign exchange spreads, and any processing or spend-management fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report worldwide business income if the company is tax resident in South Africa by incorporation or effective management. If the company is non-resident with a South African branch or permanent establishment, include only income attributable to South African-source operations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income specifically exempt from normal tax, including qualifying local dividends received or any s10(1) exemption. It is not available to operating trading receipts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents should claim exemption only where the relevant provision in s10 of the Income Tax Act applies without regard to the foreign shareholder's residence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 – Taxable Income before Assessed Loss
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income less deductions and allowances attributable to the card issuing trade. Expenses must be supported by full documentary evidence in terms of s11(a), s23, and s102 of the Tax Administration Act.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All firm-specific expenditure must be awarded to the South African tax record. Cross-border fee allocations, software royalties, and group service charges must be arm's length and disclosed in the transfer-pricing statement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Residual assessed loss brought forward from prior years, set off against current-year taxable income under s20 of the Income Tax Act.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss carryforward is available to any entity with an assessed loss, provided the trade is not deemed to have ceased and the continuity-of-trade requirements are satisfied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net amount subject to normal tax at the company rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The basis of computation is the same for resident and non-resident branches, but source rules under s9 of the Income Tax Act apply to foreign-sourced income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income multiplied by 27% for years ending after 1 April 2022.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident branches are taxed at the same 27% rate on South African sourced trading income. The company must not offset 20% dividends tax or final withholding taxes against normal tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: First, second, and third provisional tax payments made during the year of assessment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies with a South African branch must register for provisional tax and make all three payments through SARS eFiling.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of transactions with connected persons, including the issuing bank, network schemes, program managers, or group treasury companies. Attach transfer-pricing documentation and arm's length study if applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory for all cross-border connected-person transactions. The company must complete this disclosure even if no transfer-pricing adjustment is considered necessary.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late submission of the ITR14 attracts administrative penalties charged per month or part of a month that the return remains outstanding, with the monthly penalty amount determined by the taxpayer's turnover class and can escalate up to ZAR 16,000 per month for larger corporate entities. An additional understatement penalty under s223 of the Tax Administration Act may apply, ranging from 0% to 200% of the tax shortfall depending on the conduct that caused the understatement. Late payment of normal tax is subject to interest at the prescribed rate, being the South African Reserve Bank repo rate plus 3%.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% dividends tax, imposed on the beneficial owner of the dividend and collected by the company as withholding agent; the distribution amount is deemed to be net of 20% tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply the reduced dividend withholding rate under a double tax agreement (DTA), the foreign shareholder must submit to the South African paying company, before the dividend is paid, a valid SARS Declaration for reduced withholding rate (Form DTD), a Notification of Dividend (Form DTF) and a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign revenue authority. The South African company must retain these documents and may, upon receipt, withhold at the treaty rate (commonly 5%, 10% or 15% depending on shareholding percentage and DTA). Without these documents, the 20% dividend tax must be withheld and paid to SARS.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest paid to a non-resident is subject to 15% interest withholding tax (effective for interest accrued from 1 March 2015). Royalties for the use of intellectual property, software, patents, copyrights, trademarks, or card network licences paid to a non-resident are subject to 15% royalty withholding tax. Under an applicable DTA, the rates may be reduced to 0%-10% for interest and 5%-12% for royalties, subject to beneficial ownership and a valid TRC. Withholding must be declared and paid on SARS returns before or on the date of payment unless a full exemption or treaty relief is established.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Cross-border transactions with connected persons exceeding ZAR 5 million in aggregate in a year of assessment trigger the obligation to prepare, maintain, and produce contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation. A full Local File and Master File are required for multinational groups with consolidated group revenue of at least ZAR 1 billion or where the covered cross-border controlled transaction value exceeds ZAR 100 million; simplified documentation applies only to smaller low-risk businesses.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Any other OECD-authorised method that yields the highest degree of comparability
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Africa has no UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations statute, but economic substance is a live doctrine applied through the residence test (place of effective management under s1 of the Income Tax Act), the general anti-avoidance rules (s80A to s80L), the transfer-pricing provisions (s31), and controlled foreign company attribution rules (s9D). A South African Pty Ltd acting as a pure letter-box or billing shell for an offshore group strategy, without board meetings, employees, contracts, operational systems, or decision-making power in South Africa, will not qualify for treaty benefits and may face recharacterisation as a foreign resident, disallowance of deductions, deemed dividends, and severe penalties. The virtual card business must demonstrate real executive and operational activity materially performed in South Africa.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally omitting card-programme revenue, interchange fee income, cardholder subscriptions, or foreign exchange fees from the ITR14; inflating deductible expenses or depreciation; creating fictitious intellectual-property licensing costs; or back-dating assessed losses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011, an understatement penalty of up to 200% of the tax shortfall applies for intentional tax evasion. Criminal prosecution under s235 of the same Act can result in a fine not exceeding R10 million and imprisonment of up to five years. SARS also charges interest at the prescribed rate on unpaid taxes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly participate in the submission of a false tax return are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax, interest, and penalties. Personal liability recovery by SARS can extend to personal assets. Criminal prosecution may result in travel bans, extradition, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: ZA_PTY_LTD is used solely as an invoice and revenue-pass-through shell, with no real South African office, no full-time employees, no locally resident directors, no board meetings held in South Africa, no procurement of banking or IT services in South Africa, and no decision-making function in the jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SARS may recharacterise the company under the general anti-avoidance rules (s80A) and deny treaty benefits, foreign tax credits, and deductions. The company could be treated as a controlled foreign company of an offshore parent, triggering CFC attribution. Penalties include understatement penalties up to 200% of taxable income reallocated and CIPC deregistration of the entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors of a shell company may be personally liable under s77 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 for knowingly carrying on the business recklessly or with negligent intent. Directors face civil restraint orders, travel bans, and disqualification from acting as directors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorist Financing (AML/CFT) Non-Compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing virtual corporate cards without obtaining and verifying beneficial ownership of cardholders, failing to conduct enhanced due diligence on high-risk clients, failing to file suspicious transaction reports with the Financial Intelligence Centre (FIC), or allowing the card platform to be used for round-tripping, invoice fraud, or terrorist financing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001, administrative fines can reach ZAR 10 million per contravention. A conviction in a criminal court for deliberate non-reporting can result in a fine or imprisonment up to 15 years (depending on the offence), and the financial regulator may revoke the authorised payment or financial-services licence relevant to virtual card issuance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors have personal liability where they fail to install an accountable-instance control and proper AML governance. Directors may be individually fined, disqualified, and imprisoned for up to 10 years where the non-compliance was intentional or reckless.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing and Thin Capitalisation Adjustment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Undercharging cross-border interchange or processing fees to an overseas group treasury, paying excessive software licensing royalties to a connected intellectual-property owner, or financing the South African card operations with excessive related-party debt carrying non-arm's length interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SARS may adjust the consideration under s31 to reflect the arm's length price, disallow interest deductions for excessive debt, impose secondary adjustments, and apply understatement penalties of 100%-200% of the resulting tax shortfall. Interest at the prescribed rate runs from the original date of assessment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve pricing schedules or group service contracts that are not arm's length may be held personally liable for the additional tax, interest, and penalties if they knew or ought to have known that the arrangements were not justified by commercial substance. Civil recovery proceedings and travel bans are available to SARS.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Declaring dividends to a foreign parent or foreign shareholders without withholding the 20% dividends tax; making interest or royalty payments to a non-resident without withholding 15% interest or royalty tax; claiming treaty relief without supporting TRCs and DTD/DTF forms; or underreporting withholding taxes on the relevant SARS return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The company is liable for the unwithheld dividend tax, interest tax, or royalty tax as a withholding agent. SARS may collect the full 20% dividends tax payable, or 15% on interest/royalties, plus an administrative penalty of up to 10% of the unpaid withholding tax per month, and further understatement penalties. Directors face personal liability if the company failed to withhold without valid exemption documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who caused or permitted the company to pay dividends or cross-border fees without withholding are personally liable for the outstanding withholding tax. SARS may make a personal-liability assessment, issue a section 179 notification under the Tax Administration Act, and impose travel bans or obtain civil judgment for recovery.
